skill.name: bitwarden-browser-aac-login
skill.description: Use Bitwarden Agent Access CLI (`aac`) with agent-controlled browser login flows. Use when a user wants an AI agent to log into a website through `aac listen`/`aac run`, approve credentials in Bitwarden Agent Access, fill browser login forms without printing passwords, debug Agent Access browser login pairing, or build a credential-conscious bridge between `aac run` env injection and browser automation.
skill.summary: Guides consent-based Bitwarden Agent Access browser logins without exposing credentials in chat.
skill.author: arthurzakirov

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives: the external-command matches identify Markdown backticks and CLI examples, while the network matches describe loopback or placeholder URLs. The documented bridge still exposes credentials to an agent-controlled child process and browser execution, so publication requires clear user consent and strict handling of the in-memory trust boundary.

remediation.issue: The recommended bridge passes AAC-injected credentials from a child process to active browser automation.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer manual approval or a credential-blind helper; when the bridge is necessary, obtain explicit consent, bind only to loopback, use a random one-use port, avoid logs, and clean up on timeout.

remediation.issue: The workflow uses `aac run --env-all`, which exposes all selected credentials to the child process.
remediation.suggestion: Use the narrowest domain and credential scope available, avoid `--env-all` when a specific variable set is supported, and never print environment values or command output containing secrets.

remediation.issue: Browser login automation can submit consequential actions after authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the documented confirmation gate before account creation, payment, permission grants, or sensitive form submission, and verify only non-secret page state.

content.user_title: Secure Browser Logins with Bitwarden AAC
content.value_statement: Browser login automation can expose credentials when agents handle them directly. This skill provides a consent-based Bitwarden Agent Access workflow with domain checks, sanitized status, and explicit trust boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Guide users through pairing and approving Bitwarden Agent Access requests.
Define domain-scoped `aac run` login workflows for browser automation.
Keep passwords, TOTP codes, and tokens out of chat and diagnostic output.
Recommend stable browser locators and non-secret login verification signals.
Describe a temporary loopback bridge with one-use cleanup and sanitized errors.
limitations: It does not install, configure, or operate the AAC CLI by itself.
It cannot guarantee that third-party browser tools keep credentials agent-blind.
It requires user approval and a matching Bitwarden Agent Access connection.
It does not replace provider-specific login, MFA, or account recovery guidance.

use_cases.title: Approve a Website Login
use_cases.description: Guide a developer through domain verification, AAC approval, browser form filling, and non-secret success checks.

use_cases.title: Design a Credential Bridge
use_cases.description: Help an automation engineer evaluate a temporary loopback bridge, cleanup behavior, and the in-memory credential trust boundary.

use_cases.title: Document a Safe Login Runbook
use_cases.description: Create a support runbook that avoids pasted secrets, explains common AAC failures, and records sanitized outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Basic Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to use Bitwarden Agent Access for a browser login to example-app.test. List the approval and secret-handling steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Domain-Scoped Login
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step checklist for logging into example-app.test with `aac listen` and `aac run`. Include only non-secret verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Denied Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose an AAC login that reports Request denied. Use domain matching, cached connections, vault item matching, and sanitized status checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Credential Bridge
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed AAC browser-login bridge for trust-boundary risk. Require loopback binding, a random one-use port, no credential logs, timeout cleanup, and explicit user consent.

output_examples.input: The login page is open, but the AAC request was denied.
output_examples.output: Check that the approved domain exactly matches the target site, that the local listener is unlocked, and that a matching vault item exists. Do not paste the approval token or CLI output.

output_examples.input: The browser form was filled and the page changed to the account dashboard.
output: Verified by the changed page state.

output_examples.input: Should I use the temporary browser bridge for this login?
output_examples.output: Use manual entry or a credential-blind helper when possible. Use the bridge only after the user understands that credentials pass through agent-controlled memory, with loopback-only binding, no logs, and immediate cleanup.

best_practices: Confirm the exact target domain before requesting credentials.
Report only sanitized status and never print environment values or credential-bearing output.
Stop for user confirmation before payment, permission grants, or sensitive submission.
anti_patterns: Asking users to paste passwords, TOTP codes, tokens, cookies, or rendezvous codes.
Using broad credential injection without explaining the agent-controlled trust boundary.
Saving real domains, account identifiers, session values, or credentials in examples.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for Bitwarden Agent Access and browser login workflows. It does not operate the CLI or browser tool automatically.

faq.question: Should credentials be pasted into chat?
faq.answer: No. Keep passwords, TOTP codes, API keys, cookies, tokens, and rendezvous codes outside chat.

faq.question: Why must the domain be confirmed?
faq.answer: Domain confirmation limits the credential request to the website the user expects and helps prevent approval of an unintended site.

faq.question: What is the temporary bridge?
faq.answer: It is a loopback-only, one-use server that passes credentials in memory from an AAC child process to active browser automation.

faq.question: Is the bridge fully agent-blind?
faq.answer: No. The browser automation and helper can handle credentials in memory. Prefer manual entry or a credential-blind helper when practical.

faq.question: How should login success be verified?
faq.answer: Use non-secret page state, such as a changed URL, title, greeting, logout link, or expected next step.
